entry.evidence: Currently, available global hydrographies do not feature small headwater streams in great detail.

sequences.source_document: Publisher full text from XML (jats_text), with PDF for figures

steps.action: Reviewed earlier global hydrographies (HYDRO1k, HydroSHEDS/HydroRIVERS, MERIT Hydro, MERIT Hydro–Vector) and their channelisation thresholds (1000, 10, 5 and 1 km2).
steps.quote: Various DEMs have been used for global stream channelisation

steps.action: Stated the gap: no global hydrography delineates small headwater streams in detail, although headwaters are estimated to make up more than 70 % of stream length.
steps.quote: its coarse channelisation threshold does not yield a worldwide distribution of small headwater stream channels in substantial detail

steps.action: Set a uniform worldwide flow-accumulation threshold of 0.05 km2 (about six 3-arcsec cells) to initiate stream channels, arguing that higher thresholds such as 1 km2 would omit headwaters.
steps.quote: employ a standard, worldwide channelisation threshold of 0.05 km 2

steps.action: Adopted the MERIT Hydro DEM, with its published bias and noise corrections and hydrological carving, as the elevation input for all calculations.
steps.quote: As the basis for all calculations, we used the MERIT Hydro DEM

steps.action: Built the processing chain: chose MD8 (Holmgren FD8) over D8 and D-infinity, masked 1400 interior lakes and depressions, tiled the DEM (59 irregular tiles, 116 regular tiles), computed a globally seamless MD8 flow accumulation, then re-extracted streams, basins and sub-catchments with GRASS GIS and gave them global unique IDs (1.56 million basins, 726 million segments).
steps.quote: we opted for MD8 using the traditional Holmgren method

steps.action: Designed the validation: rasterised NHDPlus HR and three global datasets (HydroRIVERS, GRWL, MERIT Hydro–Vector) to 3 arcsec, buffered the NHDPlus HR lines in 100 m steps up to 400 m, and counted overlapping cells and relative stream length.
steps.quote: We then buffered the NHDPlus HR gridded stream lines in five categories

steps.action: Compared spatial overlap with NHDPlus HR. Hydrography90m had the highest overlap at the smallest buffers (46 % within 100 m) and 28 % fewer stream cells than NHDPlus HR, against 77–99 % fewer for the other datasets.
steps.quote: Within a buffer distance of 100 m, Hydrography90m overlaps with NHDPlus HR by 46 %, achieving the highest overlap among all available global hydrographic datasets

steps.action: Checked flow accumulation against NHDPlus HR TotDASqKm on 61 million cells (MAD = 0.597, rho = 0.709) and compared the areas of the 10 largest basins with HydroBASINS and HYDRO1k.
steps.quote: the comparison showed, in general, a high agreement in the basin surface area among the datasets

steps.action: Computed the topographic and topological variable layers: stream slope, distance, segment properties, five stream-order schemes, and the flow indices spi, sti and cti.
steps.quote: we produced layers that characterise the topographic and topological properties of the hydrography

steps.action: Re-ran the whole workflow several times and applied benchmarking checks: cell resolution, unique IDs, histograms for outliers, and cross-over counts (outlets = basins; segments = sub-catchments).
steps.quote: The entire procedure was run several times during computational development to check for consistency and potential mismatches among the different hydrographic layers.

steps.action: Attributed the Yangtze basin-area discrepancy (Table 2) to flow routed through the Tongji Canal and Niger routing problems to missing bifurcations, rather than revising the dataset.
steps.quote: routes sections of the Yellow's flow accumulation into the Yangtze, leading to discrepancies among the compared global hydrographic datasets

steps.action: Kept the claim that Hydrography90m represents stream networks more accurately than the three compared global datasets, crediting the DEM, MD8 and the small threshold.
steps.quote: The data validation procedures confirmed Hydrography90m as a more accurate representation of stream networks compared to HydroRIVERS, GRWL, and MERIT Hydro–Vector.

tree.answer: Small headwater streams are missing from global hydrographies
No; channels are potential flow paths derived from a DEM by flow routing
Build and characterise a global 90 m hydrographic dataset
No rival hypotheses; existing global datasets serve as comparators
Checked against NHDPlus HR (US only), other datasets and internal reruns; threshold not varied
Capability characterised: highest overlap with the reference and more headwaters
Accepted after text and usability changes; uncertainty and wet/dry analyses declined

end.claim: Hydrography90m, a global 3-arcsec hydrographic network with a 0.05 km2 channel threshold and MD8 routing, overlaps the NHDPlus HR reference more closely (46 % within 100 m) and contains more headwater channels than HydroRIVERS, GRWL and MERIT Hydro–Vector.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the globally seamless MD8 flow accumulation and the uniform 0.05 km2 threshold there would be no headwater-resolving global network to validate.

gates.evidence: No hypothesis directed data acquisition; the design goal of resolving headwaters set the threshold (§1 ¶5). The accuracy claim faced a comparison against NHDPlus HR and three rival datasets that it could have lost (§5.1 ¶3). Nothing was fixed before the data were seen; buffers and metrics are reported without pre-specification.

imports.item: Median absolute deviation, Spearman rank correlation and 2D kernel density for flow-accumulation agreement
High Performance Computing cluster with cascading Bash batch jobs and job arrays (12 418 core hours)
River Continuum Concept as the rationale for stream-order layers
2-D Fourier filtering to remove stripe noise (in the adopted MERIT DEM)

novelty_claims.quote: Hydrography90m is the first-ever data product that allows for global and comparative area-of-interest studies on small headwater stream channels.
delineating small headwater streams for the first time globally
can be considered a pioneering computational achievement
have not been depicted globally until this publication
a vital and long-overdue baseline for assessing actual streamflow in headwaters

limits: Validation covers only the contiguous United States (NHDPlus HR), so no generalization to other climates or terrains is shown. The 0.05 km2 threshold was never varied, so its effect on accuracy is not reported. A wet/dry stratification was requested by Referee 2 and declined (AC3 ¶10). The channels are potential flow paths; whether they carry water is deferred to later discharge modelling (§8.1 ¶2). The flow-accumulation check (MAD, rho) was done for Hydrography90m alone, not for the rival datasets. Table 2 shows large unexplained differences for the Ob basin (2.58 versus 3.09 million km2); only the Yangtze difference is explained (canal). Inference: NHDPlus HR also uses a 10 m DEM for flow accumulation, so its independence as a reference is partial. The repeated runs (§7 ¶2) are reported without their results. Sub-claims: basin-area agreement with HydroBASINS and HYDRO1k (capability_characterized, qualitative 'high agreement'); flow-accumulation agreement (estimate_with_resolution, MAD 0.597, rho 0.709, Figure 10). The citation correction requested by Referee 2 is incomplete: §5.1 ¶1 of the published PDF (p. 4535) still cites Lin et al. (2019) for MERIT Hydro–Vector. Composition none_fits: the walk is gap, then build, then validate against a reference and comparators. Capability_first does not fit because the question precedes the capability and no phenomenon is established; there are no rival hypotheses.

disagreements.support: Its 1 km2 initial threshold is argued to miss headwaters, and in the validation it had 77 % fewer stream cells than NHDPlus HR.
disagreements.quote: its coarse channelisation threshold does not yield a worldwide distribution of small headwater stream channels in substantial detail

disagreements.target: Messager et al. (2021) global non-perennial river map based on HydroRIVERS
disagreements.support: The paper argues from the larger channelisation threshold; it gives no direct test of that map.
disagreements.quote: small headwater streams are nevertheless missing from this dataset because of a significantly larger stream channelisation threshold

disagreements.target: D8 routing as used in HydroRIVERS, MERIT Hydro and MERIT Hydro–Vector
disagreements.support: Cites the artificially straight channels of D8 and the acknowledgement by Yamazaki et al. (2019) that D8 is inadequate in headwaters; the paper adopts MD8 instead.
disagreements.quote: it is acknowledged that D8 algorithm is not adequate for representing flow contributing area in headwater regions

disagreements.support: In the buffer overlap against NHDPlus HR these datasets show lower overlap and 77–99 % fewer stream cells.
disagreements.quote: the Hydrography90m has the highest lateral accuracy within the smallest buffer ranges among each of the compared [...]

disagreements.support: Argues that planned discharge-based monthly pruning would represent the network better; no evidence is shown in this paper.
disagreements.quote: than assigning, for example, a channelisation threshold contingent on the geographic region alone, as suggested by

alternatives_considered.chosen: MD8 multi-flow direction (Holmgren FD8 in GRASS GIS)
alternatives_considered.reason: D8 gives artificially straight channels and is inadequate in headwaters; MD8 is implemented in GRASS GIS and performs similarly to D-infinity in flat terrain

alternatives_considered.chosen: Uniform 0.05 km2 flow-accumulation threshold, with later dynamic pruning by discharge
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Higher threshold (e.g. 1 km2); region-dependent threshold (Vogt et al. 2003); pruning with a wider threshold from the start
alternatives_considered.reason: Higher thresholds would omit headwater features and prevent computing headwater stream variables

alternatives_considered.chosen: Regular tiling system of 116 tiles of 20° x 20° for distribution
alternatives_considered.reason: Avoid handling and distributing a computationally heavy global file

alternatives_considered.chosen: Exclude NHDPlus HR streams inside lakes (masked with HydroLAKES)
alternatives_considered.reason: Artificial straight 'fish-bone' channels caused by zero slope
